title: Judge orders LSU to roster RJ Luis, clearing him to play despite SEC rule
content:
After a year and a half away from college basketball — and despite an SEC rule preventing him from playing this season — RJ Luis is closer than ever to returning to the court.

An East Baton Rouge judge granted Luis a preliminary injunction Friday that enjoins the SEC from “giving effect to any penalty or threat of penalty by the SEC, its Commissioner, or the NCAA,” according to the court filing. The judge also ordered LSU to roster Luis, clearing the path for the former St. John’s star to suit up for the Tigers as soon as next week.

“The intent of the judge’s ruling is to ensure that RJ Luis Jr. is put on the roster,” Elliot Abrams, one of Luis’ attorneys, told The Athletic. “He did that because the court has already found that with 13 of the 16 SEC teams having actual professionals on their teams, it is arbitrary and capricious — and therefore likely unlawful — to prevent a person who has never played a professional game from being rostered on the ground that he, of all these people, is too professional.”

After winning Big East Player of the Year in 2024-25, Luis declared for the 2025 NBA Draft but went unselected. The 6-foot-7 wing signed a two-way contract with the Utah Jazz, was later traded to the Boston Celtics, but never appeared in an NBA regular-season game.

The SEC previously argued that Luis is ineligible because he signed contracts with NBA teams. But in October, the same judge issued Luis a temporary restraining order (TRO) that prohibited LSU, the SEC and/or SEC commissioner Greg Sankey from declaring Luis ineligible.

Even after that TRO, though, LSU opted not to roster Luis. Coach Will Wade — in his first season back at LSU after the school fired him on the eve of the 2022 NCAA Tournament for multiple alleged NCAA infractions — said at the SEC’s preseason media day that he would “follow all the SEC protocols” when it came to Luis.

Testifying virtually from Spokane, Wash., Friday ahead of the Tigers’ game Saturday at No. 14 Gonzaga, Wade said the only reason he hadn’t rostered Luis yet was out of fear of retribution from the SEC.

But Friday’s ruling now forces Wade to roster Luis — who averaged 18.2 points and 7.2 rebounds in his final season at St. John’s — while seeming to protect him and LSU from any related fines, suspensions, or other sanctions.

The filing explicitly prohibits LSU, the NCAA, the SEC and Sankey from “refusing to allow RJ Luis Jr. to be a member of the LSU men’s basketball team and to practice, participate, and compete with the team throughout the 2026-27 season.”

“The question now is going to be for the presidents of the SEC schools, whether they will comply with the law,” Abrams said. “If they comply with law, then they will leave RJ Luis, coach Will Wade and LSU alone.”

Luis, the 2025 Big East Player of the Year, did not travel with the Tigers to Gonzaga and could not fly to Spokane independently on Friday night because of the FAA’s nationwide ground stop.

Abrams said he “absolutely” anticipates Luis to suit up for LSU in the immediate future.

LSU did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

While the judge ordered LSU to roster Luis, that does not mean Wade has to play him. But if he and the Tigers are protected from punishment for playing Luis, there’s seemingly no reason why Wade wouldn’t want to add another dynamic perimeter piece to his team, which has started the season 3-0.

LSU is averaging 94 points per game, albeit against vastly inferior competition, while looking every bit like an NCAA Tournament team.

With Luis in tow too — if Wade decides to play him — then there’s no telling how dangerous the Tigers can be this season.
